title: The Educated Barbarian: Hagakure analysis (part. 15)
summary: NH continues reading Hagakure, commenting on doing what you enjoy, dreams, limits projected onto others, dignity in appearance, merit over birth, intentional action, contrarian logic, continuous improvement, fear of obstacles and integrity against the crowd. He applies several passages to training choices and physique.
claims: Life is short so do what you enjoy; people faking a passion are easy to spot because they have no fire
In training nothing is truly optimal; an exercise you like that is 75% optimal beats a 100% one you will not do, because the 75% is actually realized
To remember dreams keep paper by the bed and write them on waking; dreams reflect your state of mind and are underrated
People project their own limits onto others; those who failed assume everyone will, a coping mechanism driving society's mediocrity
Idolizing people creates an artificial ceiling that blinds you to anyone surpassing it
A limitation is just the absence of knowledge about what lies beyond it
Appearance reflects who you are because you choose to train, to be overweight or not, to be clean; you cannot complain about being judged on those choices
Calm, humility and graciousness may look external but stem from within
Greed has covertly become an accepted ideal; most people say their dream is to be rich
Bravery is increasingly criticized through its link with masculinity
We love the self-made underdog, and class should be something you can rise out of
Being born wealthy does not make you bad, but those given everything who waste it deserve contempt
Intention shown through demeanor makes crowds part: walk looking straight ahead and people give way
Like punching through a board rather than at it, intention carries the motion
Nothing gets resolved by postponing; action gets things done
People hiding something tend to babble fast to avoid gaps in conversation
Mentally arguing the opposite of what you hear trains logic and makes you harder to manipulate, but can slide into circular sophistry if intentions are impure
Form and content differ: the same message can be phrased countless ways; aim for the one perfect phrasing
Always keep improving; in anything competitive, people pass you as soon as you stop
Entertainment helps recovery and relaxation but becomes a problem when it replaces information or real effort
Anything can be achieved through training, but the effort, time and focus you put in dictate the return; work hard and smart
Aim very high; the higher the goal the more you strive and progress
Obstacles feed on fear you created; once you accept a goal as impossible it becomes impossible
Many people's moral compass simply copies the crowd's
He cites an elevator conformity experiment where strong-willed subjects faced the right way while low scorers copied the group
Keep negativity to yourself; crowd-driven praise and criticism are fake and cowardly
Stick to your opinions even against a thousand people; lack of integrity is what makes someone not a warrior
